title: The Group Robustness is in the Details: Revisiting Finetuning under Spurious Correlations
measurement_description: The paper evaluates model robustness to spurious correlations related to religious identity (Christian, Muslim) within the CivilComments dataset, a benchmark for toxic comment classification. Religion is treated as a spurious feature that can lead to performance disparities for minority groups.
findings: In the context of the CivilComments dataset, where religious identity is a spurious feature, the paper found that common class-balancing techniques like upsampling can cause a 'catastrophic collapse' in worst-group accuracy, harming performance on minority groups (including religious ones). The paper also showed that model scaling can improve robustness for these groups, but only when paired with appropriate class-balancing techniques. Furthermore, it identified a 'spectral imbalance' where features from minority groups exhibit a larger spectral norm, potentially exacerbating performance disparities.
